title: LIFX bulb cannot connect to home WiFi
shortDescription: Setup completes but bulb fails to join the home WiFi network.
fullDescription:
LIFX bulbs run their own WiFi setup AP. During setup, your phone connects to the bulb's AP, you enter your home WiFi credentials, and the bulb attempts to join. Failures usually come from 5GHz-only networks (LIFX is 2.4GHz only), special characters in the password, or WPA3 mode.

Split-band networks where 2.4 and 5GHz share an SSID often work. Mesh routers with band-steering can confuse the bulb during the moment it tries to switch.

causes.cause: Router MAC filter blocking new device

symptoms: App says 'failed to connect to your network'
Bulb returns to slow pulsing white after setup
Bulb visible briefly then disappears from app

fixSteps.title: Confirm 2.4GHz
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure your WiFi has a 2.4GHz band enabled and is using WPA2-PSK (not WPA3).

fixSteps.title: Disable mobile data
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off cellular data on your phone before starting setup so it does not jump off the LIFX AP.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset bulb
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle wall power 5 times (on 2s / off 2s). Bulb will cycle colors confirming reset.

fixSteps.title: Try simpler password
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily set router password to a simple alphanumeric to rule out character issues.

faq.a: No. All current LIFX bulbs are 2.4GHz only.

title: Bulb works locally but cloud features fail
shortDescription: App control works at home but Alexa/Google/away-from-home does not.
fullDescription:
LIFX bulbs maintain a persistent connection to the LIFX cloud (cloud.lifx.com). When this fails, scheduled effects, voice control, and out-of-home control fail while LAN control still works.

This is usually DNS, ISP routing, or LIFX cloud outage.
symptoms: Cloud icon grayed out in LIFX app
Schedules do not run when away

fixSteps.title: Check status page
fixSteps.instruction: Visit https://status.lifx.com to verify outages.

fixSteps.title: Reboot bulb
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle wall power once and wait two minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reauth voice assistant
fixSteps.instruction: In Alexa or Google Home app, disable then re-enable the LIFX skill.

videoSearchQuery: LIFX cloud offline alexa not working

faq.q: Can I use LIFX without cloud?
faq.a: Yes, locally via the LIFX LAN protocol or HomeKit on supported models.

title: Bulb pulsing amber/orange after setup
shortDescription: Bulb is in setup mode and not joined to WiFi.
fullDescription:
A slow amber pulse indicates the bulb is in factory/setup state and broadcasting its setup AP. This is normal on first power-on, but if it persists after setup, your credentials never saved.

Return to LIFX app > Add Light to retry.
symptoms: Bulb visible as LIFX_xxxx access point

fixSteps.title: Run setup
fixSteps.instruction: Open LIFX app > Add Light. Follow on-screen instructions to join 2.4GHz WiFi.

fixSteps.title: Verify password
fixSteps.instruction: Type WiFi password into a notes app first to confirm characters before re-running setup.

faq.a: No, it means the bulb is awaiting setup.

title: Bulb flashing red, in firmware recovery mode
shortDescription: Bulb pulses red because firmware update was interrupted.
fullDescription:
If a firmware update is interrupted (power loss, app crash), LIFX bulbs enter a red-flash recovery mode. The LIFX app should detect them automatically and offer to repair the firmware over the air.

If the app does not detect, factory-reset the bulb with five power cycles.
symptoms: Bulb does not respond to app commands

fixSteps.title: Open LIFX app
fixSteps.instruction: The app should auto-detect the bulb in recovery mode and offer to reflash firmware. Follow prompts.

fixSteps.title: Manual reset
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle wall power 5 times (on 2s / off 2s). Bulb returns to setup mode.

whenToCallPro: Replace under warranty if recovery fails.

faq.a: Yes, after factory reset all customizations are gone.

title: Connected bulb does not appear in LIFX app
shortDescription: Bulb is online but not visible in the app.
fullDescription:
If the bulb is online (white light) but not visible in the LIFX app, your phone may be on a different network segment or the LIFX app cache is stale.

LIFX uses UDP discovery on port 56700; this is broken by client isolation, VPNs, and many guest networks.

causes.cause: Phone on guest network or VPN

symptoms: Bulb works in Alexa but not LIFX app
Refresh in app does not detect bulb

fixSteps.title: Disable VPN
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off any VPN and switch off mobile data.

fixSteps.title: Same network
fixSteps.instruction: Connect phone to same SSID and band as bulb (2.4GHz).

fixSteps.title: Reinstall LIFX app
fixSteps.instruction: Delete and reinstall LIFX app, sign in again.

faq.q: Why does Alexa work but LIFX app does not?
faq.a: Alexa uses cloud control; LIFX app prefers local LAN.

title: Bulb dims itself due to overheating
shortDescription: Bulb reduces brightness automatically when too hot.
fullDescription:
LIFX bulbs include a thermal sensor and reduce brightness when internal temperature exceeds safe limits. Common in fully enclosed fixtures or when wattage rating is exceeded.

The bulb is functioning correctly; the fixture or environment is the problem.
symptoms: Bulb hot to touch when off

fixSteps.title: Check fixture rating
fixSteps.instruction: Verify fixture is rated for the bulb wattage and is open or vented.

fixSteps.title: Move bulb
fixSteps.instruction: Try the bulb in an open fixture to confirm thermal throttling.

whenToCallPro: If you need to replace an enclosed fixture.

faq.a: Repeated overheating shortens lifespan even with throttling.

title: Bulb does not appear in Apple Home
shortDescription: HomeKit pairing fails or bulb shows as unresponsive in Home app.
fullDescription:
LIFX HomeKit pairing requires a HomeKit code from the box or LIFX app. If the bulb was previously paired to another HomeKit home, it must be reset before re-pairing.

The LIFX app provides a 'Reset HomeKit' option per bulb.

causes.cause: Bulb already paired to old Home

fixSteps.title: Reset HomeKit
fixSteps.instruction: LIFX app > select bulb > Settings > Reset HomeKit. Then re-add via Home app.

fixSteps.title: Check Home Hub
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm an Apple TV, HomePod, or iPad is online as Home Hub.

faq.q: Do all LIFX bulbs support HomeKit?
faq.a: Most do; check the box for the HomeKit logo.

title: Visible bands or zones on LIFX Z/Beam strip
shortDescription: Sections of the LED strip show wrong color or are dark.
fullDescription:
LIFX Z and Beam are zone-addressable. If a zone is dark or wrong color, a connector may be loose, the strip may be cut at the wrong spot, or the controller has remapped zones after a reset.

Reseat all connectors and re-run zone setup in the app.
symptoms: All zones offset by one position

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, unplug each connector, blow out dust, reconnect firmly.

fixSteps.title: Re-detect zones
fixSteps.instruction: LIFX app > strip settings > Detect zones.

videoSearchQuery: LIFX Z strip dead zone fix

faq.q: Can I extend a LIFX Z strip?
faq.a: Yes, up to 10 meters with extension kits.

title: Bulb offline after power outage
shortDescription: After a power outage, bulb fails to rejoin WiFi.
fullDescription:
Some routers come back online slowly after an outage and assign new IP ranges. LIFX bulbs occasionally fail to renew DHCP and stay offline.

A quick power cycle of the bulb after the router has fully booted resolves it.

causes.cause: DHCP not yet ready when bulb booted

symptoms: Bulb dim or off after outage

fixSteps.title: Wait for router
fixSteps.instruction: After power restoration, wait 5 minutes for router to fully boot.

fixSteps.title: Cycle bulb
fixSteps.instruction: Toggle wall switch off 10 seconds, on. Bulb rejoins network.

videoSearchQuery: LIFX bulb offline after power outage

faq.q: Should I assign a static DHCP lease?
faq.a: Yes, a reservation in your router improves reliability.

title: Animations or effects look choppy
shortDescription: Spooky/Color Cycle effects skip or freeze briefly.
fullDescription:
LIFX effects run on the bulb itself but rely on stable WiFi for sync across multiple bulbs. Stutter usually points to weak WiFi RSSI or contention with other 2.4GHz devices.

Moving the access point closer or switching the bulb to a less congested AP fixes most cases.

fixSteps.title: Check signal
fixSteps.instruction: LIFX app > bulb > diagnostics. RSSI better than -65 dBm preferred.

fixSteps.title: Set 2.4GHz channel
fixSteps.instruction: Set router 2.4GHz to channel 1, 6, or 11 with no auto-switching.

whenToCallPro: Network installer if WiFi coverage is fundamentally insufficient.

faq.a: No, they run on-bulb but multi-bulb sync uses LAN.
